newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends weak as U.S. gasoline slides.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends weak as U.S. gasoline slides.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended the week on shakey ground after coming under pressure from tumbling U.S. gasoline prices, dealers said.
After plunging to a session low of $17.88, June Brent steadied slightly to close 32 cents down at $17.97 a barrel, more than cancelling out modest midweek gains.
Dealers said much of the day's slide was caused by profit-taking on NYMEX heating oil contracts and selling of gasoline-to-crude crack spreads.
"We've seen a fair bit of selling of the gasoline and heating oil cracks in the U.S.," said a broker.
Despite depleted gasoline stock levels in the U.S., dealers remain unconvinced that prices can hold current levels amid evidence that demand is running only very slightly above last year's levels.
NYMEX June gasoline lost over two cents a gallon.
Earlier, IPE gas oil closed sharply weaker, the prompt May contract sliding $5.50 to $165.50 a tonne.
The prompt May/June intermonth spread was also under pressure, losing 75 cents to stand at a slim 25-cent backwardation, partly under pressure from a deterioration in physical market sentiment.
Traders said Asian arbitrage opportunities were looking less attractive amid slower demand in Singapore and a smaller than expected June purchase tender award from the Indian Oil Corp.
